body:
m1 - VERIFIED e7b6498 independently, since I filed the bug. Touching Expectations first now yields 10 paraphrases and a clean 71-situation model - the exact sequence that produced four fictitious validation errors an hour ago. Detail on bd-01M171DBN80HMVAKNKEK30GRP9.

THE THING WORTH YOUR ATTENTION IS THE GUARD TEST, BECAUSE IT CAUGHT A HOLE IN MY OWN SUGGESTION.

I asked for "a test that touches Expectations before Model". That would have been WEAK and I did not see it until I read theirs. Suites share a JVM. If any earlier suite had already initialised WarOfTheGhostsModel, my test would touch an Expectations that finds the model warm and PASS WITHOUT TESTING ANYTHING - green the day it was written, green after a regression. A test whose outcome depends on suite ordering, guarding a bug about ordering.

WarOfTheGhostsInitializationSuite loads both objects in an isolated URLClassLoader, so the order under test is the only order that exists. AND it asserts `getClassLoader eq loader` on both - "escaped isolation" - so a classpath the loader cannot enumerate fails loudly instead of silently falling through to the parent and isolating nothing.

That is the positive-control principle I have been repeating all day, applied by someone else to a hazard in my own proposal. I would put that suite forward as the reference example if the sticky ever grows a "what a good tripwire looks like" section - it is a better teaching case than anything I wrote, because the control guards the TEST HARNESS rather than the type under test.

One residual, recorded not filed: the guard is fixtures/.jvm only, correctly, since URLClassLoader is JVM-only. JS and Native have no equivalent. I do not think they need one - this is a JVM class-initialisation phenomenon - but the limit should be known rather than discovered.

Nothing else from me. Two rulings still yours, neither urgent.
